en.title: Rivers and lakes
en.summary: The main rivers and lakes and the language of flow and length.

paragraphs: Rivers and lakes shape the landscape and the cities beside them. This lesson describes the main ones and teaches the vocabulary of flow, length and position.

The River Thames flows through London into the North Sea and is about 346 kilometres long. The Severn is the longest river in the UK, and the Lake District in north-west England has many lakes, including Windermere, the largest in England. In Scotland a lake is called a loch, and Loch Ness is the best known. In North America, the Great Lakes lie between Canada and the United States, and the Mississippi is the main river of the United States. A guide on a boat on the Thames speaks to tourists.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: The Thames flows through London and into the North Sea.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.text: Is it the longest river in Britain?

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: No, the Severn is longer. The Thames is about 346 kilometres long.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: The Lake District has many, including Windermere, the largest in England. In Scotland they are called lochs.

lines.speaker: Tourist
lines.text: Is it possible to swim in the Thames?

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: In some places, yes, but you must check the water quality first.

paragraphs: **1. Flow into, flow through and rise in.** These verbs describe the course of a river. See Introduction to Grammar: Prepositions and conjunctions.

blocks.html:
FormExample
flows throughThe Thames flows through London.
flows intoIt flows into the sea.
rises inIt rises in the Cotswolds.
runs alongThe path runs along the river.

paragraphs: **2. Length and width with adjectives.** The measurement comes before the adjective: 346 kilometres long. See Introduction to Grammar: Adjectives.

blocks.html:
FormExample
346 kilometres longThe Thames is 346 kilometres long.
10 metres deepThe lake is 10 metres deep.
the length ofthe length of the river
the largest inthe largest lake in England

items: Loch is the Scottish word for a lake.
The Great Lakes lie between Canada and the United States.
The Mississippi is the main river of the United States.
A bank is the side of a river; a bridge crosses it.

paragraphs: Rivers have shaped the position of cities such as London, York and New York. Boat trips and riverside walks are popular with visitors, and the river is a main part of city life.
